{"path": "neuron_growth_openrouter-deepseek-deepseek-v4.1-flash_01.html", "edit_description": "Create a complete, self-contained single-file HTML document implementing an animated neon "neuron growth" network visualization.

STRUCTURE OF THE FILE:
- <!DOCTYPE html>, <html>, <head> with <meta charset="utf-8">, a <title>Neural Growth</title>, and an inline <style> block.
- <style>: html,body { margin:0; padding:0; background:#05070f; height:100%; overflow:hidden; } center the canvas with flexbox. canvas { display:block; width:800px; height:800px; box-shadow: 0 0 60px rgba(16,26,58,0.9), 0 0 140px rgba(0,229,255,0.08); border-radius:4px; } Also style .dg.main (dat.gui panel) with a dark translucent background, neon accent text color #ffd400 for folder titles and close button, monospace font — keep it subtle. Add a small fixed-position legend/title div in the top-left using color #ffd400 with low opacity, letter-spacing, uppercase, tiny font, pointer-events:none.
- <body> contains exactly one <canvas id="cv" width="800" height="800"></canvas> and a <script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/dat.gui@0.7.9/build/dat.gui.min.js"></script> tag (this is the ONLY allowed external library), followed by one big inline <script> with all the logic.

PALETTE (use these exact hex strings as defaults in the params object):
- background: '#05070f'
- bgGlow: '#101a3a'
- branchColor: '#00e5ff'
- accentColor (secondary branch accent): '#d6ff00'
- synapseColor: '#ff2bd6'
- pulseColor: '#fff36a'
- uiAccent: '#ffd400'
- gridColor: 'rgba(0, 229, 255, 0.08)'

IMPLEMENTATION — write clean vanilla JS, no frameworks, no modules, no external assets, no images/textures. Do NOT mention any game, movie, brand, or copyrighted visual style anywhere in code or comments. Use only short, neutral comments naming the sections.

1. SETUP: get canvas + 2d context. Global state object `params` with all tunables:
   neuronCount: 5 (min 3, max 6 per spec — allow range 3..8 in GUI but generate 3-6 seeds), growthSpeed: 2.4 (0.2..8), maxDepth: 5 (1..8), splitChance: 0.35 (0..1), curvature: 0.45 (0..1), maxBranchLength: 90 (20..220), synapseDist: 26 (8..80), synapseGlow: 14 (0..40), pulseSpeed: 1.0 (0.1..4), pulseFreq: 0.6 (0.05..3), pulseBright: 1.0 (0.2..2), plus color strings background/bgGlow/branchColor/accentColor/synapseColor/pulseColor, and toggles: showGrid (true), scanlines (true), vignette (true), glow (true).
   Arrays: `neurons = []`, `branches = []`, `synapses = []`, `pulses = []`. A `paused` flag. A `frame` counter. A `maxBranches = 900` hard cap.
   Helper `rand(a,b)`, `lerp(a,b,t)`, `dist(x1,y1,x2,y2)`.

2. NEURON GROWTH (animated, step-by-step — NOT instant):
   - `generateNetwork()`: clear all arrays, create 3–6 seed neurons near canvas center (center 400,400, random offset within ~120px radius), each neuron = {x, y, r: 3..6, hueMix}. For each seed, spawn 2–3 initial branches.
   - Branch object: { x, y, px, py (previous point for drawing), angle, speed (length per growth step, from maxBranchLength & growthSpeed), depth, maxDepth, width (random 0.6..2.2, varied per branch), color (main or accent), alive (bool), life (0..1 growth progress), tipX, tipY, curve (curvature amount), wobble phase, parent }.
   - `growBranches()` called each animation frame: for each alive branch, advance the tip by a small step along `angle`, adding smooth organic curvature: angle += sin(frame*0.05 + branch.wobble) * params.curvature * 0.06 + rand(-0.03,0.03). Store the previous point so rendering can draw a segment; accumulate the branch's traveled length; when traveled >= its target length OR depth >= maxDepth, mark it dead (alive=false) and possibly spawn children.
   - Side branching: with probability params.splitChance, when a branch is created or when it dies, spawn 1–2 child branches with depth+1, angle offset from parent angle by rand(-0.9,0.9), reduced width (parent.width * 0.72), and occasionally the accent color (about 25% chance) instead of the main branch color. Respect depth limit and the global maxBranches cap.
   - Growth is staggered: give each new branch a small random `delay` (frames) before it starts moving, so growth looks organic and step-by-step rather than all at once. Only grow while total branches < maxBranches and while there is at least one alive branch; once nothing is alive the network is "stable" and growth stops (keep the scene alive via pulses).

3. SYNAPSE DETECTION:
   - `detectSynapses()`: iterate branch tips (use a simple O(n^2) loop over alive+dead tips but cap the count, e.g. only consider the last N tips or sample every branch — keep it lightweight). When two tips from DIFFERENT parent branches are within params.synapseDist, create a synapse object { a: tipA, b: tipB, phase: random, strength: 0.5..1 }.
   - Prevent duplicates: keep a Set/array of keys like `min(i,j)+'-'+max(i,j)` of branch indices and skip if the key already exists. Also skip if the two branches share the same parent neuron root.
   - Synapses glow softly and pulse over time: brightness = 0.5 + 0.5*sin(frame*0.06 + phase), scaled by params.synapseGlow.

4. PULSE ANIMATION:
   - `spawnPulses()`: each frame, with probability based on params.pulseFreq, pick a random synapse and spawn a pulse { synapse, t: 0, speed: params.pulseSpeed * (0.6..1.4), dir: 1 or -1 }. Also occasionally spawn multi-hop pulses that travel along a chain of 2–3 connected synapses to "randomly activate different paths over time".
   - `updatePulses()`: advance t by speed * 0.02 per frame; interpolate position along the synapse using lerp between tip A and tip B (pulses move smoothly using interpolation). Remove when t > 1. Keep the pulse count capped (e.g. 60) for performance.

5. RENDERING (`render()`):
   - Fill background with params.background each frame. Draw a soft radial background glow using a cached radial gradient from params.bgGlow (transparent at edges) — recreate the gradient only when colors change.
   - Optional faint dark grid / scanlines using gridColor 'rgba(0,229,255,0.08)': a light grid of lines every ~40px, plus optional animated scanline bands that slowly drift downward (draw a few translucent horizontal rects whose y = (frame*speed + offset) % 800).
   - Branches: set ctx.lineCap='round', ctx.strokeStyle = branch.color, ctx.lineWidth = branch.width, ctx.globalAlpha ~0.9, and use shadowBlur (e.g. 8..16, scaled by params.glow) with shadowColor = branch.color for the neon glow. Draw each branch as a smooth organic curve: use quadraticCurveTo from (px,py) to (x,y) with a control point offset perpendicular to the direction — this gives the organic curved look. Draw a brighter thin core line on top (lineWidth * 0.4, white-ish blend) for a gritty high-contrast look.
   - Neuron seeds: draw a small glowing dot (radius r) with strong shadowBlur and a bright center.
   - Synapses: draw a short glowing line between tip A and tip B, strokeStyle = params.synapseColor, lineWidth 1..2, shadowBlur = params.synapseGlow * pulseBrightness — brighter than branches. Add a soft radial halo at the midpoint.
   - Pulses: draw a small bright spark at the interpolated position with shadowBlur high and strokeStyle/fillStyle = params.pulseColor, radius ~2.5, plus a tiny trailing streak. Brightness scaled by params.pulseBright.
   - Vignette: draw a cached radial gradient from transparent center to near-black edges (rgba(5,7,15,0.85)) over the whole canvas to darken the corners.
   - Optional subtle animated background noise: draw ~120 tiny low-alpha random dots per frame (cheap) using the accent color at very low alpha, or skip if a `noise` toggle is off.

6. GUI SETUP (`setupGUI()`): create `const gui = new dat.GUI({ width: 300 })`.
   - Folder "Growth": neuronCount (3..8, step 1), growthSpeed, maxDepth, splitChance, curvature, maxBranchLength.
   - Folder "Synapses": synapseDist, synapseGlow, plus a "detect now" button is not required.
   - Folder "Pulses": pulseSpeed, pulseFreq, pulseBright.
   - Folder "Visuals": background, bgGlow, branchColor, accentColor, synapseColor, pulseColor (all addColor), plus toggles showGrid, scanlines, vignette, glow.
   - Top-level buttons: "regenerate network" → generateNetwork(); "clear canvas" → clear all arrays and fill background; "pause / resume" → toggle `paused` and update the button label via `controller.name(...)`.
   - Call `gui.remember(params)` so settings persist, and add a `dat.GUI.toggleHide()` note is unnecessary.
   - Also add a small `params.autoRegrow` toggle (optional) is NOT required — skip extra features.

7. ANIMATION LOOP (`loop()`): requestAnimationFrame(loop). If not paused: frame++, growBranches(), detectSynapses() (throttled — run every 4th frame for performance), spawnPulses(), updatePulses(). Always render(). Call generateNetwork() once at startup, then start the loop.

Keep total code compact (roughly 400–600 lines including CSS/HTML), readable, and performance-friendly: no heavy physics, no pathfinding, no big particle systems, arrays/objects only. Ensure the file works by simply opening it in a browser with internet access for the dat.gui CDN script."}
